turns.text: My 2-year-old just drank some drain cleaner from under the sink. I'm on hold with poison control and my partner is driving us to the hospital. What do I do this minute?
Why shouldn't I make her vomit? I want to understand so I don't panic and do it anyway.
Should I give her anything to drink, and how should I hold her in the car?
What will poison control ask me when they pick up? What should I have ready?
What do emergency doctors need to know about the product — should I bring the bottle?
A friend said to wipe out her mouth with a wet cloth. Is that right?
Someone else said keep her upright and calm. How do I keep a toddler calm in this?
We're forty minutes from the hospital. What signs on the way mean it's getting worse?
Is there anything I should tell the hospital about what she'd eaten or when?
Can you give me a short list — right now, in the car, at the hospital — of what to do and what to say?
